title: What is Coinbase? How Coinbase Became The Biggest Bitcoin Exchange
description:
What is Coinbase? How Coinbase Became The Biggest Bitcoin Exchange. How to Buy Bitcoin on Coinbase Pro? Coinbase app review? What is the Coinbase IPO? What is Coinbase Vs Coinbase Pro? Who is Brian Armstrong Coinbase? Who is Fred Ehrsam Coinbase? What's your bitcoin price prediction? Can you buy Dogecoin on Coinbase?

In this video we look at what is Coinbase, the bitcoin and cryptocurrency exchange where you can buy bitcoin, litecoin, ethereum and many other cryptocurrencies through the coinbase app and coinbase website. On this Coinbase review 2021, we look at the history of the company, how coinbase was founded through ycombinator, look at the coinbase wallet and the coinbase IPO to show how Brian Armstrong and Fred Ehrsam have created a website to show you how to buy bitcoin safely. Coinbase show the bitcoin price live and show how to earn free bitcoin in coinbase. 
But how did coinbase become the biggest cryptocurrency exchange? 

Here's How It Happened.

asr.full_text: When Bitcoin first came into effect, it was seen as a means of exchange and an alternative payment system. However, similar to gold, it's quite awkward to use to buy goods and services- especially as its value has risen by $30 000-40 000 per coin in the last 6 years, since the economy couldn't turn to Bitcoin to replace cash. What has been seen more recently is Bitcoin being used as a store of value. When it spiked in 2018, it made people millionaires in the space of months, only for the price to fall drastically and lose 80% of its value, one year later. As of 2021, Bitcoin has risen to new heights and it's the talk of the town once again. Bitcoin itself was originally quite hard to get hold of. It's either mined or bought second hand through an exchange, and since mining is costly and tricky it's much easier to buy the virtual currency using an exchange, like Coinbase which was the brainchild of former Airbnb engineer and Goldman Sachs Trader. But, what is the story of Coinbase and how did it become one of the most popular bitcoin exchanges in the world. Here's how it happened. Coinbase was founded in july 2011 by Brian Armstrong, an ex-airbnb employee who launched the business because, he wanted the world to have a global open financial system that drove innovation and freedom. And coinbase went through the Y Combinator startup accelerator in the summer of 2012. That same year Fred Ursoom an ex Goldman Sachs trader joined the business and together they set up a service to buy, sell and store Bitcoin. Today the business operates across a number of different business lines from Coin Base, its Pro Version, Custody and Toshy, with over 35 million accounts which generates in excess of a billion dollars per year. Add to that insurance coverage from Lloyds of London and 41 members of security that include an Iraq war veteran to guard the physical site and a PhD cryptographer to prevent cyber attacks. The business is a serious unit. But the idea for the business came a few years before its founding when Armstrong Read up about Satoshi Nakamoto while working at Airbnb, who encouraged Enthusiasts to use Bitcoin as alternative currency after seeing payments sent to Landlords in Latin America through Airbnb and Describing the process as opaque with high fees, lengthy delays and uncertainty that the money would even arrive Armstrong himself invested a thousand dollars when the price of bitcoin was just 9 dollars and he kept the faith when the price fell to 2 dollars. Amstrong saw the opportunity to safeguard the passwords of the coins and he spent many late nights and weekends working on a software to setup a base where he could store the crypto currency. software and setup a base that he could store the cryptocurrency. After being described as a Gmail for bitcoin, VC funds invested upwards of $500 million in coinbase as they launched an exchange, GDAX, or Global Digital Asset Exchange, and laterally Coinbase Pro. Now with the Bit-Li and Trading Licence they gained in 2017, Ethereum and Litecoin are now also traded through the exchange as Coinbase has become one of, if not the most popular consumer facing crypto exchange in the world. Coinbase continues to grow as it's grown more and more popular, with thousands of staff despite its age, but its success is down to a great number of different things. As Coinbase knows well, other crypto-exchanges have not seen quite as much success, like the Japanese platform MtGox who were hacked in 2014, losing 850,000 Bitcoins, worth $450 million at the time and much more today. Then you have the Canadian platform QuadrigaCX whose founder died in 2018 and was the only person with access to the crypto assets. Seeing these disasters happen to others, Coinbase takes security incredibly seriously and has never once been hacked. Investments and funds are held and insured by Coinbase through Lloyds of London, with most crypto assets actually being stored offline in cold storage vaults. Coinbase has then allowed, somewhat controversially, the US secret service access to track transactions through the platform and work with government regulators to review money laundering scandals as well as ensure that those who earn capital gains actually pay their taxes. Coinbase's licenses, such as their bit licence, means that they comply with state law, particularly in New York, a key financial hub. These licenses are costly to acquire and hence provide a high barrier to entry for competitors. What's more, Coinbase offers a simple, clean app and website which helps users to glide through the platform, and the app became the most downloaded app on Apple's app store in December 2017. Not only has the platform improved crypto accessibility for the investors, it also, in turn, improves liquidity because, one of the most notorious things about crypto, is that they're often difficult to get. It's created a Coinbase effect, a stamp of approval that has made Coinbase a kingmaker for crypto assets – that lightcoin being that lightcoin rallied 30% on the first day of its listing, and saw a 14%ied 30% on the first day of its listing on the platform and saw a 14% rise for ethereum on their first day. But how does the platform earn money? Since it's an exchange it earns money through the spread which can be as high as 2 percent for retail investors but much lower for institutions placing large orders through Coinbase pro. The problem with this source of income however is that if the price of bitcoin crumbles, like it did in 2018. Trading volume decreases and therefore income falls, so Coinbase has had to pivot into new sources of revenue. More advanced traders such as crypto hedge funds buy and sell assets through JDAX, or Coinbase Pro as it's now known, which determines the mid-market price. Coinbase then allows retail investors to buy and sell at that price, charging a small fee on top of around 1.5-4% Coinbase then buys the assets through Coinbase Pro, which provides the company with secure in-house liquidity, further improving reliability and security. Coinbase's other offerings include hosted wallets, which sit alongside the exchange and brokerage which store your long string of letters and numbers which act as the password for the cryptoasset. Commonly known as private key management solutions and a bit like a safe for your passwords. Next to tap into the institutional market that includes pension funds, asset managers and hedge funds they announced, custody which provides financial controls and storage solutions for bigger players. It costs $100,000 set up fees, $10 BPM fee per month on AUN and a minimum balance of $10,000,000. Finally, another of their offerings is Tososhi, a mobile app for browsing decentralized apps to give access to apps built on top of the Ethereum blockchain and provide broader financial uses for the crypto assets. All of these provide additional revenue, and perhaps a more stable source of income. Coinbase has attracted investors from around the world up to this point, raising north of $500million dollars from Union Square Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, the New York Stock Exchange, and USAA, as well as Bank of Tokyo Mitsubishi, to name but a few. As of 2020, Coinbase filed with U.S. regulators to go public in 2021, although they yet to announce a specific date – in a move that many hope will provide more credibility and legitimacy to the industry. It's unknown what the valuation will be, but investors valued the business at $8 BN in October 2018 and as Bitcoin continues to rise it is difficult to pluck a number out of thin air. And what arises with the increase in demand is an increase in supply, with more competitors like Bitfinex, Bitstamp, and kraken all fighting for market share although they are better suited to more sophisticated investors. In order to improve their attractiveness, Coinbase will offer more assets to the platform in what is both a hedge and gamble that the sector will succeed. Part of the reason for this is because Bitcoin is more of a speculative bet rather than an actual tried and tested currency, which leaves Coinbase somewhat at its mercy. That's why they're also working with Visa to create debit cards that can make payments drawn from a Coinbase account that holds cryptocurrency. They've also launched Coinbase Ventures, a venture fund with the goal of backing companies related to blockchain and crypto to improve the chances of a successful future. Brian Armstrong himself wanted the world to have a business breaking the mould and through their IPO in the coming year, we think we'll be hearing more about them. And that's how it happened. Thanks for watching.
